findings.file: decision_document / Decision / UAR-side stream fixes and History
findings.claim: The decision depends on changing UAR behavior without establishing that this project can modify or require those UAR-side changes.
findings.evidence: The decision puts in scope: "UAR-side stream fixes (in scope): emit TEXT_MESSAGE_START/END ... signal lagged subscribers" and later "UAR change: accept host-supplied history on the runs API". The constraints identify an external/reference repository as untouchable: "Reference only (`project.json` → `workspace`). Never written, including its worktrees." The packet does not state that UAR itself is writable in this phase or that a released UAR version with these API changes will exist before the-boss commits to this integration.
findings.suggested_fix: Split host-only decisions from UAR API changes, and add an explicit dependency/version gate: the-boss integration may only ship against a UAR release that exposes the required stream markers, lag signaling, action route behavior, and host-supplied history API.

findings.claim: The decision claims to cover "ALL" UAR features but reduces multiple features to run-trace display rather than functional support.
findings.evidence: The scope table says "everything else UAR emits (skills activated, memory, guardrails, sycophancy, budget, context, sub-agents, citations) | this decision (run-trace parts)". The original intent asked for "full support ... and ALL the features it provides". Persisted `data-uar-*` run-trace parts are only described as compact telemetry display, not as support for configuring, invoking, enforcing, or round-tripping those features.
findings.suggested_fix: Define what "support" means per feature: display-only trace, host-controlled configuration, UAR-controlled execution, persistence, replay, user settings, and failure behavior. Do not mark a feature covered by this decision unless its operational path is specified and falsified.

findings.claim: A load-bearing renderer compatibility assumption remains unchecked even though the decision says it was locally checked.
findings.evidence: The header says the revision followed "a local check of the official A2UI renderer", but the assumptions say "The official `@a2ui/react` renders UAR's catalog correctly with the-boss's own components ... not yet run." The decision commits to `@a2ui/react` 0.10.2 and writing 9 components before this compatibility is executed.
findings.suggested_fix: Run the minimal renderer spike before committing: install the exact package version, render all 9 UAR-emitted component APIs under both catalog IDs inside the-boss's React bundle, and record the result as evidence rather than an assumption.

findings.claim: The 50 ms rendering threshold is arbitrary and tied to one machine, so it cannot falsify whether the design is viable for supported platforms.
findings.evidence: The falsifier requires "re-renders each update within 50 ms on the operator's development machine". The original intent explicitly targets platform support across "windows arm/x64, macos arm/x64, linux, etc.", and the constraints include a Windows verification warning. No source is given for 50 ms and no platform or hardware matrix is specified.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace this with platform-specific budgets or a rationale-derived threshold, and include at least the slowest supported platform class or mark the decision blocked until cross-platform performance is measured.

findings.claim: The restart falsifier only checks conversational text recall, not whether UAR stateful features survive restart.
findings.evidence: The decision states "UAR's session context is in memory only and has no history route" and proposes to "re-send history". The falsifier only requires that after killing the sidecar, the reply "uses the earlier turns' content". That does not test restored skill activations, memory state, guardrails, budget/context state, A2UI surfaces, pending approvals, or sub-agent state—the same features the scope table claims are covered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add restart fixtures for at least one active A2UI surface, one pending/declared action, one tool approval state, one selected skill, and one memory/context artifact; require either exact restoration or explicit user-visible degradation.

findings.claim: The assumption that "a continuation run appearing as a new turn" is acceptable is not actually falsified by the round-trip test.
findings.evidence: The assumption says "A continuation run appearing as a new turn is an acceptable experience for A2UI replies." The falsifier only checks that "the continuation run appears as a new turn". It verifies the chosen behavior occurs, not that it is acceptable or preserves A2UI interaction semantics.
findings.suggested_fix: Define acceptance criteria for A2UI action UX: whether the action updates the originating surface, creates a new assistant turn, preserves focus/context, and remains understandable in history. Test those criteria instead of only checking that the implementation does what the decision already chose.
